subject: grayWolf
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: gray wolf standing alert.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
I'm planning a compact but solid wolf module—forward-facing, stylized with chunky shoulders, big paws, and a ruff, and sketching out the skeleton hierarchy starting from the hips joint.

Defining spine, neck, head, jaw joints...

For coloring I'll use a countershaded wolf coat with mottled greys and a cream underbelly blending via gradient. Then I'm sweeping a neck path up to the head with a tapering radius, and adding a mane by scattering flattened spike cones outward along the neck surface for a ruff effect.

Now I'm building the head: a part-sphere skull, frustum-box muzzle and jaw, spherical nose, cone ears, and textured plane decals for amber slit eyes, positioning everything relative to the head's local forward/left/up axes so it faces correctly.

No mirroring needed for the decal. Now working out the leg rig: setting shoulder and paw positions for the front legs, checking that the two-bone limb lengths roughly match the reach distance, and naming the joint chain so it parents correctly to the spine—though the reach is slightly short, which will force the leg to straighten.

For the hind legs, I'm computing hip and foot positions with digitigrade bends (knee forward, hock back) across three segments, making sure the total bone length comfortably exceeds the hip-to-foot distance, and assigning names for hip, knee, hock, and foot so the four-point limb chain lines up correctly.

For front legs I'm sweeping tapered tubes along the shoulder-elbow-paw chain with decreasing radii, then adding paw spheres with small forward-pointing claw spikes, and anchoring each leg's root joint to the correct spine position with lateral offset for left/right sides.

Adding small teeth cones in the jaw, a banded tail sweep with a dark tip, and a jagged dorsal mane of dark spikes running along the back using spike placement along the body sweep's normals. I'm also giving it a simple leather collar with a fang pendant instead of armor, keeping the Warcraft flavor without overcomplicating the geometry.

Now I'm building out the skull and muzzle geometry, positioning the head frame off the neck joint, scaling a sphere for the skull in local head coordinates, and starting the frustum shape for the muzzle.

Adding facial colors, fang spikes, and ear geometry...

For the eyes, I'm planning an amber ellipse with a slit pupil and angular brow slant, mirrored for left versus right sides, plus small cheek ruff spikes positioned around the jaw.

I'm skipping shoulder tufts and setting up a grey color palette with countershading and mottling for the coat, extending that same treatment to the legs.

For the tail, I'm darkening the tip with a banded color gradient. For body shape, I'm defining radius functions along the chain that taper width and height from rear to chest, shifting the profile slightly downward, and I'm about to work out the neck sweep next.

Neck curve runs from shoulder up to head position, pitching upward toward an alert head pose; checking proportions against a real wolf's shoulder height and overall body length to make sure scale feels right. Now I'm sizing up the hind thigh mass as an ellipsoid at the hip joint.

Adding shoulder mass and chest ruff spikes, then building paw geometry as flattened spheres positioned at the foot tip joints with careful offsets so they sit flush on the ground, plus small forward-pointing claw spikes at the toes.

Now I'm setting up the limb chains as polylines passed into a sweep function, assigning tapering radii along each leg so the hind legs get a smooth decreasing thickness from hip to foot.

I'm figuring out side-naming conventions for mirroring joints (L/R), deciding to pose the jaw open slightly at the end after all the jaw geometry exists so the parts move rigidly together, and keeping the tail low for an alert wolf stance. I'm also planning to scatter dorsal spikes along the body sweep using a spike-generating helper at sampled points.

Then I'm adding bigger spikes along the neck sweep, and scattering a cream-colored chest ruff by sampling points on the body surface filtered by normal direction and spacing, attaching small cone shapes to each point. Finally, I'm wrapping up by writing the metadata export.
